reason: The text establishes and emphasizes multiple hierarchical structures: (1) Divine hierarchy—God commands Moses and Aaron, with explicit authority relationships; (2) Leadership hierarchy—Moses is appointed God's representative to Pharaoh, with Aaron positioned as his prophet/spokesperson ('Aaron your brother will be your prophet to you'); (3) Priestly hierarchy—extensive genealogies of the Levites and Aaron's priestly line establish hierarchical succession through family lineage; (4) Structural emphasis—the genealogical lists establishing 'heads of fathers' houses' (ראשׁי בית אבתם) underscore family-based authority structures. The text assumes and reinforces hierarchical ordering as a fundamental organizing principle, particularly through the appointment of Moses and Aaron to authority over the Israelites and the detailed enumeration of priestly lineage.
